slides.title: std::array & std::span Concept
slides.prompt: std::array is a fixed-size stack-allocated wrapper around C-style arrays. std::span (C++20) provides a lightweight non-owning view over any contiguous sequence.

slides.title: std::array Declaration
slides.prompt: Fill in the non-type template parameter defining the size in std::array.

slides.title: std::array Memory Overhead
slides.prompt: What is the memory overhead of std::array<T, N> compared to a raw C array T[N]?
options: Zero overhead; it has the exact same size and stack layout as raw C-array T[N]
Contains an extra 8-byte pointer for size tracking
Requires dynamic heap allocation header overhead
Contains a virtual function table pointer
slides.correctAnswer: Zero overhead; it has the exact same size and stack layout as raw C-array T[N]

slides.title: std::array Fill Method
slides.prompt: Fill in the method used to fill an std::array with a specific value across all elements.

slides.title: std::span Non-Owning Nature
slides.prompt: What happens if the underlying buffer viewed by a std::span is destroyed?
options: std::span becomes a dangling view; accessing it results in Undefined Behavior
std::span extends the lifetime of the underlying data automatically
std::span makes a copy of the data before destruction
A runtime exception is thrown immediately
slides.correctAnswer: std::span becomes a dangling view; accessing it results in Undefined Behavior

slides.title: std::span Subspan
slides.prompt: Fill in the method returning a sub-view of the first N elements of a span.

slides.title: Passing Contiguous Buffers to Functions
slides.prompt: Why is std::span<T> preferred over const std::vector<T>& in function parameters?
options: std::span can accept C arrays, std::array, std::vector, or any contiguous buffer seamlessly without copies or allocation
std::span is faster because it uses multi-threading
std::span allows resizing the caller's container inside the function
std::vector references are deprecated in C++20
slides.correctAnswer: std::span can accept C arrays, std::array, std::vector, or any contiguous buffer seamlessly without copies or allocation

slides.title: Dynamic Extent Span
slides.prompt: What is std::dynamic_extent when working with std::span?
options: A default template value indicating the span size is determined at runtime
A flag that allocates heap memory dynamically
An error state returned when span is empty
The maximum size limit of stack memory
slides.correctAnswer: A default template value indicating the span size is determined at runtime
